notes: Step 1 parts were correct; no parts added or dropped.

Circuit (from image and schematic): 5V to + rail to photoresistor to the A0 junction; the 10k resistor runs from that junction to the - rail (GND). Pin 9 goes to the LED anode, the LED cathode goes to the 220 ohm resistor, and the resistor goes to the - rail.

Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue (top half = bank 't', rows a-e), although the image labels that half f-j. Column numbers are read from the image: photoresistor in columns 6 and 10, 10k resistor in columns 10 and 13, LED in columns 22 and 23, 220 ohm resistor in columns 23 and 26. The row letter within a column strip is arbitrary.
Rail hole numbers (tp.1, tn.2, tp.4, tn.13, tn.26) are approximate. Each rail is a single strip, so the electrical result does not depend on them.

The LED's bent (longer) leg is taken as the anode, in column 22 with the blue pin-9 wire. The cathode in column 23 goes through the 220 ohm resistor to GND. In the schematic the resistor sits before the LED, but they are in series, so the circuit is equivalent.
The manual's line 'Analog sensor on Analog input 2' contradicts the rest of the page. The text, schematic and image all use A0, so A0 is used.
The photoresistor is used as the analog sensor, as the manual's parts list suggests.
